subject: Civil Engineering
title: Curing: Keeping Concrete Wet
description: Learn Curing: Keeping Concrete Wet in one minute.

hook.text: Pour concrete and walk away — it cracks. Curing is the step most people skip.

buildup.text: Hydration needs water. If the surface dries out, the reaction stops and cracks form.

discovery.text: Wet curing keeps the surface moist with burlap, water sprays, or ponding for 7 days.

twist.text: Curing compounds — sprayed-on membranes — seal moisture in when wet curing isn't practical.

climax.text: Properly cured concrete can be 50% stronger than uncured concrete from the same batch.

punchline.text: Concrete needs babysitting. Keep it wet and it rewards you with strength.

quiz.question: Why must fresh concrete be kept moist during curing?
options: To wash away excess cement from the surface
Water is needed for the hydration reaction that creates strength
To prevent the concrete from absorbing contaminants from the air
